surfaces.part: seat/back plank lying on its side (light vertical stem)
lower bar (leg/back) top with 2-row dark front

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a sideways H/I shape. The light stem (rows 3-10 at x=8, L 166-200) and the upper bar (rows 3-4) are flat lit surfaces seen from above. Only 1-2 dark rows (row 5 at x=11, rows 11-12 at x=8 and x=4) are drawn as a front face under them. That is fewer than 3 rows of vertical south face and no solid front under the seat surface, so the object reads as a flat top-down slab, not a three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny toppled chair of about 14x12 px with only 10 distinct colours in total. Its chair parts read as roughly 2 tones, a light tan and a dark brown, with very little highlight or mid-tone ramp. The wood strokes are flat, with no grain dots or per-plank highlights, unlike the bench reference, which shows several wood steps and plank grain. The outline is dark and mostly tinted brown, but it is thin and used uniformly, so it reads as a sticker-like silhouette. The measured facts of 0 visible tones per tile and 0% near-flat coverage only mean the piece is smaller than a tile, so they do not count for or against it. Judged by eye, it is clearly thinner and flatter than the bench, which is the closest reference. A careful artist would not accept it next to the references without it looking shallower.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny toppled chair of about 10 distinct colours. It shows roughly 3 lightness steps on the wood: a light top edge, a mid tone and a dark brown. The measured facts are 0 per tile and 0% flat, because the piece is smaller than one tile, so they say nothing here and I judged by eye. answer.evidence: The toppled chair is drawn as a flat, almost top-down silhouette: a wide upper bar (rows 2-5), a narrow light strip (rows 5-9, width 5), and a lower bar (rows 10-13). The light seat/strip colour (L=200, rows 5-8 at x=8) is a flat plane with no front-edge line and no eave shadow. The only face below it is the darker rows 11-12 (2 rows) before the outline at row 13. No ellipse or roof plane is present, and the front face is under 3 rows, so it reads as a flat slab and not a 3/4 view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny toppled chair, smaller than one tile, and it has only 10 distinct colours. By eye the wood is built from about 3 steps: a light top edge, a mid tone and a dark outline/underside. It has no visible grain, no per-plank highlights and no texture dots. The bench reference is also small and sparse, but it shows clearer plank highlights, a darker underside and leg shading, about 5 steps. The outline pixels lean brown and are not neutral (0% near-neutral), so this is not a sticker outline. The facts show no flat-fill coverage, but the piece is thin and reads flatter than the bench next to it. A careful artist would find it simpler and less shaded than the bench, and richer references such as the well and the stall are far ahead. When in doubt, fail.
